triples.subject: Fyodor Pavlovitch
triples.quote: suspecting that she would go to Fyodor Pavlovitch in his absence, he returned at last to the town, to find, to his joy, that she had not been near his father.

triples.subject: Mitya
triples.quote: Here Ippolit Kirillovitch described at length the prisoner’s fatal passion for Grushenka.

triples.subject: Fyodor Pavlovitch
triples.quote: At the same time the prisoner’s father was captivated by the same young person—a strange and fatal coincidence, for they both lost their hearts to her simultaneously

triples.subject: Mitya
triples.quote: when he knelt before her, stretching out hands that were already stained with the blood of his father and rival.

triples.subject: Mitya
triples.quote: by means of that very three thousand roubles, which the son looked upon as his own property, part of his inheritance from his mother, of which his father was cheating him.

triples.subject: Mitya
triples.quote: Then the prosecutor went on to describe how the idea of murdering his father had entered the prisoner’s head, and illustrated his theory with facts.

triples.subject: Smerdyakov
triples.quote: At this point Ippolit Kirillovitch broke off to discuss exhaustively the suspected connection of Smerdyakov with the murder.

triples.subject: Mitya
triples.quote: But note, frantic as he was, he took with him a brass pestle. Why that? Why not some other weapon?
